news.title: News
news.content:
Imagine you have to use an app to register your attendance with your face. First, the system shows a box on the screen so you know exactly where to put your face. As you adjust, it turns green to let you know you're ready.

It's important to be in a well-lit place. Once your face looks good, the system asks for a small gesture, like blinking or moving your head a little, to make sure it's not a photo or something fake.

The best part is that the scan doesn't take long, just about two or three seconds, and immediately a clear message appears on the screen saying whether the attendance was recorded or if there was a problem. Everything is designed to be quick and easy: open the app, press the button to go to the Facial Scan section, position yourself in the box, blink, and within seconds your attendance is saved.

termsModal.title: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
termsModal.s1Text: These Terms and Conditions govern the use of the FaceAttend EDU mobile app, which you use to check and record your attendance, submit excuses and manage your biometric authorization. By signing in you accept these terms and the Privacy Notice.
termsModal.s2Text: The educational institution of your campus is the controller of the data of its students, instructors and staff. FaceAttend EDU acts as processor: it operates the platform and processes the data on behalf of the institution and under its instructions.
termsModal.s3Text: Your account is created and managed by your institution; in the app you only sign in with your username and password. On first sign-in you must change the initial password. You can enable two-step email verification and recover your password with a temporary code. You are responsible for safeguarding your credentials and for what is done with them. The app uses the camera for facial recognition and sends push notifications.
termsModal.s4Text: We process identification and contact data (name, ID, email, phone, address, date of birth), account and security data (username, encrypted password, IP and session dates, two-step verification), attendance data and excuses with their supporting documents, alerts and push-notification tokens, and, only if you authorize it, biometric data (face and fingerprint templates). Blood type is optional health data: if you provide it, the mobile app may use it as an identity verification question when facial recognition fails. Excuses and their supporting documents may also contain health data that you choose to provide.
termsModal.s5Text: We use the data to identify and authenticate you, record and check attendance, process excuses, send alerts and reports, ensure security and prevent impersonation, and comply with legal obligations. We do not use them for advertising or sell them.
termsModal.s6Text: Biometric and health data are sensitive. Authorizing their processing is optional: you may refuse without losing access to the platform and your attendance will be recorded by other means. We store an encrypted mathematical template, not the photo. You can revoke the authorization from your profile and the template is permanently deleted.
termsModal.s7Text: If you are under 18, we only process your data with the authorization of your parent or legal guardian, which a school administrator records when your guardian comes to the school in person, and which the institution keeps, taking into account your best interests and your prevailing rights. Your biometric and health data are never mandatory. Until this registration is complete you cannot use the features that require accepted terms or facial verification. Your guardian may exercise your rights and revoke their authorizations.
termsModal.s8Title: 8. YOUR RIGHTS AND HOW TO EXERCISE THEM
termsModal.s8Text: You may know, update and correct your data, access it free of charge, request proof of your authorization, be informed about its use, revoke it and request deletion of your data when there is no legal or contractual duty to keep it. Exercise them from your profile or through your institution's contact: queries are answered within 10 business days (extendable by 5) and claims within 15 (extendable by 8). If you are not satisfied, you may go to the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce.
termsModal.s9Text: To operate, the institution uses providers that process data only on its behalf: hosting and database (Neon and AWS), the web app (Vercel), phone notifications (Expo) and email (Gmail). Some may process data outside Colombia (for example, in Brazil or the United States), under contracts requiring adequate protection. We only hand data to authorities that legally require it.
termsModal.s10Text: We apply encryption in transit and, at rest, to the ID number, email, phone, blood type, biometric templates and excuse supporting documents, role-based access control and audit logs. We keep data while you are linked to the institution and for as long as the law requires; biometric verification logs are deleted after 90 days. No system is infallible: if an incident affecting your data occurs, the institution will handle it and inform the authority and data subjects as required by law.
termsModal.s11Text: You agree to provide truthful information, not impersonate others, not try to bypass facial recognition or security measures, and not use the service for unlawful purposes. Misuse may lead to account suspension.
termsModal.s12Text: We strive to keep the service available, but interruptions may occur. We are not liable for failures beyond our control or for unauthorized access caused by improper safekeeping of credentials, except in cases of willful misconduct or gross negligence and without affecting the data subjects' inalienable rights. Facial recognition can fail; therefore the institution must offer an alternative way to record attendance.
termsModal.s13Text: We may modify these terms. If they change significantly we will let you know and, when the Privacy Notice is updated, we will ask you to accept it again.
termsModal.s14Text: These terms are governed by the laws of Colombia, especially Law 1581 of 2012 and its regulatory decrees (Decree 1074 of 2015). Disputes are subject to Colombian jurisdiction.
